findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add `cli_overrides_for('llm')` plumbing to `_parse_slot`/`load_class_slots` so the CLI layer is honored for the new slots (matching the stated 'EXISTING layered config' precedence), OR explicitly document in the Approach that CLI override is deliberately excluded for structured slots and state the accepted limitation.
evidence: Plan: 'parsed from the EXISTING layered config (config.py:388-398: CLI `-c llm.KEY` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > config file > default)'
`_parse_slot` calls `_env_override` and `raw.get(...)` but never `_root_config.cli_overrides_for('llm')`
`load_class_slots` calls `_read_llm_file_table` but not `cli_overrides_for`
Existing `LLMConfig.from_env` uses `cli = _root_config.cli_overrides_for('llm')` and passes it to `_llm_str` — the pattern is established but not followed here
findings.finding: The plan claims the new slots use 'the EXISTING layered config (CLI -c llm.KEY > REBAR_LLM_<KEY> env > config file > default)' but the implementation (`_parse_slot`, `load_class_slots`) never consults `_root_config.cli_overrides_for('llm')` — so `rebar -c llm.frontier.model=gpt-4o` is silently ignored. The CLI layer is absent from the mechanism despite being cited in the stated precedence. No AC or test exercises this layer for the new slots.
findings.location: Approach section, paragraph: 'parsed from the EXISTING layered config (config.py:388-398: CLI `-c llm.KEY` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > config file > default)'; src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py _parse_slot / load_class_slots
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar -c llm.frontier.model=gpt-4o ...` expecting the frontier slot to pick up gpt-4o; it is silently ignored and the file/default value wins instead.
The inconsistency is invisible in CI because no test covers the CLI layer for the new slots — the AC only specifies an env-var test.
findings.suggested_fix: In `load_class_slots`, retrieve `cli = _root_config.cli_overrides_for('llm')` alongside `_read_llm_file_table`, then thread the relevant nested CLI values (e.g. `cli.get('frontier', {})`) into `parse_class_slots` so the CLI layer is honored. Alternatively, add a one-sentence scope note: 'CLI override (`-c llm.*`) is not supported for nested slots; use env vars (`REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL`) or the config file instead.'
